adv_1_redis_down.method: brew services stop redis (full disconnect, 6s window)
adv_1_redis_down.expected_per_actual_contract: redis=fail + status=degraded + 200 (lenient V1 — only ALL-FAIL triggers 503)
adv_1_redis_down.actual_observed: HTTP 500 Server Error HTML page (NOT a JSON response, NOT a structured fail)
adv_1_redis_down.root_cause: The 'api' middleware group includes 'throttle:api' (app/Http/Kernel.php:'api' group). Laravel's RateLimiter resolves Cache::store(), which uses CACHE_DRIVER=redis. When redis is down, the rate limiter throws an unhandled PHP exception BEFORE the request reaches HealthzController. The try/catch blocks inside HealthzController::checkRedis() only protect the redis probe; they cannot protect against middleware-chain failures upstream.
adv_1_redis_down.impact: An uptime probe is supposed to be the LAST endpoint that fails. UptimeRobot/Cronitor will see a 500 with HTML body instead of parseable JSON. Monitors that match on 'status:"fail"' or 'checks.redis:"fail"' will MISS the actual incident — they'll show 'server-down' instead of 'redis-down', muddying the on-call paging signal.
adv_1_redis_down.recommended_fix: Either (a) remove the 'api' middleware group from /api/healthz (assign explicit empty middleware), OR (b) keep throttle but use a memory-only RateLimiter for this route, OR (c) cache the throttle state in file driver, OR (d) wrap the entire HealthzController dispatch in a try/catch that emits the same JSON schema with all checks=fail + 503. Recommended: option (a) — uptime probes should bypass auth, rate-limit, CSRF, and session middleware by design.

adv_3_queue_1000_jobs.method: inserted 1000 rows into DB::table('jobs') via tinker (chunked 100 per insert)
adv_3_queue_1000_jobs.secondary_finding: HealthzController::checkQueuePending() reads DB::table('jobs')->count(). This is the DATABASE queue driver's table. The production env has QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis (verified via .env), so real-world pending jobs accumulate in REDIS lists (`queues:default`, `queues:high`, etc.), NEVER in DB::table('jobs'). In production: queue_pending will ALWAYS report 0 even when the redis queue is overflowing.
adv_3_queue_1000_jobs.impact: The owner-facing 'queue_pending' graph in UptimeRobot/Cronitor will be permanently flat-at-zero, hiding queue backlog incidents.
adv_3_queue_1000_jobs.recommended_fix: Switch to driver-aware probe: `Queue::size('default') + Queue::size('high')`. Laravel's Queue::size() works for redis, database, and sqs drivers. Adds ~1ms latency.
